brief: Citadel Securities (Frank Flight) argues the 2026 midterms bring three macro effects: tougher AI capex conditions, a possibly faster Iran resolution, and a political shift to the centre before 2028. Electoral backlash against data centres (56% of voters called AI and data centres a major voting factor, and most local ballot initiatives opposed development) puts roughly 45 GW across 350 projects in Texas, Ohio, Pennsylvania and Georgia at risk through 2030, including 24 GW in Texas. Capital's geographic mobility should still limit the hit to aggregate AI investment, even as relocating projects delays deployment and raises costs. The bank expects a peak-AI-capex rotation out of memory, neoclouds and energy into staples, healthcare, banks, housing, retail and the hyperscalers, with hardware suppliers, especially memory and optical, exposed to deferrals while cloud operators with energized compute gain pricing power. Separately, the scale of the Republican defeat and Trump and Vance blaming the Iran war for losses could raise Washington's urgency to settle, aligning with Tehran's incentive to monetize leverage. Brent's three-month $120 upside probability has already more than halved since October 28, from 23% to 9%. The bank expects lower yields, and sees centrist Democrats outperforming, lifting DeSantis's 2028 nomination odds while denting Vance's.
